newsitem.title: GERMANY: Krupp workers protest planned job cuts.
newsitem.headline: Krupp workers protest planned job cuts.

text.p: About 1,200 workers at German steelmaker Krupp Hoesch Stahl AG on Tuesday downed tools to start a 24-hour protest against plans to cut costs by laying off 20 percent of the workforce.

The company's supervisory board planned to meet on Wednesday to consider management's plan to eliminate 2,200 of Krupp's 10,000 jobs. The workers want management to invest in modernising the Dortmund plant to preserve the jobs.
Krupp workers in Bochum also planned to drive in more than 300 cars to the supervisory board meeting in an effort to halt layoffs at their location.
A week ago Dortmund workers stopped working during an hour-long protest against the planned reorganisation.
Krupp is the steel unit of Fried. Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp.
